Smart working is an emerging phenomenon that can be understood as the use of technology and social systems to support work roles that are unique to individuals.
smart systems should be designed with the needs of the individual in mind, and that smart systems should support sustainable organizations.

the socio-technical aspects of smart working and how these aspects can be used to create meaningful and sustainable organizations.
the development of socio-technical approaches to the analysis and design of smart systems in order to support sustainable organizations.
how the smart systems of the future might be designed to promote sustainability and meaningful work.

socio-technical perspectives on smart working are essential for the creation of meaningful and sustainable systems, and that the socio-technical approach is a useful tool to support design of smart systems.
smart systems can be used to create meaningful, sustainable systems, but only if they are designed to do so.
socio-technical approaches to organizational analysis provide a useful framework for the development of smart working systems, which are sustainable in the long term.

the paper is a call for a more human-centered approach to the design of smart systems.
smart technologies should not be seen as a panacea, but as tools to be used in the context of a wider socio-technical system.
smart technologies can be harnessed to support sustainable organizations if they are designed and used in a socio-technical manner.

smart systems are only sustainable if they are developed and implemented in the context of an understanding of the unique and complex social, cultural, and organizational factors that influence their use.
